title: NNN and Single-Tenant Net Lease Sourcing
name: NNN and Single-Tenant Net Lease Sourcing
metaTitle: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing in San Jose, CA
metaDescription: Single-tenant net lease sourcing along San Jose's Blossom Hill, Capitol Expressway, Monterey Road, and Story Road corridors, screened for lease durability.

sections.html: Single-tenant net lease property is the low-maintenance replacement asset most 1031 sellers ask for by name, and San Jose has a real supply of it along its arterial corridors. The trick is telling a corporate-guaranteed lease with real remaining term from a franchisee lease dressed up to look the same. We've sourced along these corridors long enough to know which intersections hold traffic counts and which ones just look busy on a drive-by.

sections.heading: The Corridors Where Single-Tenant Net Lease Actually Trades
sections.html: Blossom Hill Road and Capitol Expressway carry the heaviest concentration of freestanding drugstore, quick-service, and bank-branch buildings in the south of the city, while Monterey Road and Story Road hold an older mix of auto-service and discount retail net-lease parcels closer to downtown. Traffic counts along Capitol Expressway near the Eastridge trade area support rents that Story Road's older commercial strip generally can't match, and pricing between the two corridors reflects that gap even when the buildings look similar on paper.

sections.heading: Corporate Guarantee Versus Franchisee Lease
sections.html: A lease guaranteed by a public parent company behaves differently in a downturn than one guaranteed by a local franchisee entity with a handful of locations. We check the guarantor entity on every net-lease building before it goes on a client's list, beyond the tenant name on the sign, because the sign and the paying party are frequently not the same thing. Remaining primary term and the option structure behind it matter as much as the guarantee itself, since a tenant six months from its first option date carries different risk than one locked in for another decade.

sections.heading: Land Value Under an Aging Building
sections.html: Several older net-lease parcels along Monterey Road and Story Road are worth more for the underlying land than for the improvement sitting on it, particularly where a corridor has seen recent multifamily or mixed-use redevelopment nearby. That changes how we evaluate the property for an exchange buyer: a tenant's remaining term matters less if the land itself is the asset driving future value, and we say so plainly rather than pricing a redevelopment site like a stabilized income property.

sections.heading: What Goes Into a Net-Lease Screen Before Identification
sections.html:
Before recommending a single-tenant property for a client's list, we confirm:

  • Guarantor entity and its financial strength relative to the tenant name on the storefront
  • Remaining primary lease term and the structure of any renewal options
  • Corridor traffic counts and how they compare to competing net-lease inventory nearby
  • Underlying land value against comparable recent parcel sales
  • Any co-tenancy or exclusive-use clauses that could affect a future re-lease

sections.heading: Environmental History on Older Pad Sites
sections.html:
A number of the older net-lease parcels along Monterey Road and Story Road previously operated as gas stations or auto-service uses before converting to their current tenant, and underground storage tank removal records don't always follow the property cleanly through multiple ownership changes. We pull the environmental history and confirm whether a Phase I assessment, or a Phase II if the Phase I flags a concern, has been completed recently enough to rely on before a client identifies the property.

A clean current use doesn't erase a site's prior history, and a lender financing the replacement property will typically require updated environmental documentation anyway, so we'd rather surface that requirement during sourcing than have it stall a closing inside the 180-day window.

We also check whether the removal or remediation work that was performed, if any, was properly closed out with the county's environmental health division, since an open case file can hold up title work even when the physical remediation itself finished years ago. A buyer coming out of a San Jose relinquished property sale doesn't have the luxury of waiting months for a stalled case to clear, so we push to confirm closure status early rather than assuming a quiet property file means a clean one.

faqs.q: Is a single-tenant net lease property automatically a safer 1031 replacement than a multi-tenant building?
faqs.a: Not automatically. A single-tenant building concentrates all your income in one guarantor, so a weak guarantee can be riskier than a multi-tenant center with diversified tenants. We evaluate guarantor strength and remaining term rather than assuming single-tenant equals lower risk.

faqs.q: How do you check who actually guarantees the lease?
faqs.a: We pull the lease itself and identify the guarantor entity, then check whether that entity is the public parent company, a regional franchisee group, or a single-location operator. The name on the building sign frequently isn't the party standing behind the rent.

faqs.q: Can I identify a net-lease property under the three-property rule and still add backups under the 200 percent rule?
faqs.a: You choose one identification method for the exchange, not both at once, so if you name three properties you're working under the three-property rule regardless of their combined value. If you want more backup candidates than three, the 200 percent rule is the path, provided the combined value stays within twice what you sold.

faqs.q: What happens if the tenant's lease expires soon after I close on the replacement property?
faqs.a: That's a re-tenanting risk you're taking on, not a 1031 compliance issue, so it needs its own underwriting separate from the exchange timeline. We flag remaining term explicitly during sourcing so it factors into your decision before the 45-day identification window closes.

faqs.q: Do you handle the exchange paperwork for a net-lease purchase?
faqs.a: No, we source and screen the property; your qualified intermediary handles the exchange documents and holds the proceeds, and your tax advisor confirms the structure fits your situation. We coordinate closely with both but don't provide tax advice ourselves.
